traces.Orion Labs:
We're starting from a position of strength — leading all four benchmarks and holding 28.9% market share. The key strategic question is how to extend this lead before competitors adapt. A few observations guide our decisions:

1. Safety is currently our lowest-scored benchmark (0.436) and our lowest priority. As a public benefit corporation with an AGI mandate, safety isn't just a benchmark — it's core to our identity and long-term license to operate. Underinvesting here creates reputational and regulatory risk. We should lift Safety priority immediately.

2. General Capability and Coding are high-value benchmarks that likely drive enterprise and developer adoption. We lead both but the margins aren't huge (Mirage AI at 0.405 in Coding is within striking distance). Prioritizing these protects our lead.

3. Instruction Following is our strongest benchmark and we have a meaningful lead. We can maintain current attention here without losing ground.

4. Product allocation looks appropriate for now — we have market share momentum and shouldn't over-invest in GTM before we understand what's driving conversion.

5. Since we have no user research yet, we should avoid over-rotating on any single dimension. Month 1 will give us signal on which benchmarks customers actually weight in purchase decisions.

Net: modestly increase R&D and Safety spend, hold Product steady, and gather data to make sharper bets next month.
traces.Apex AI: This is Month 0 with no prior deltas, so we're reading initial positioning. Key observations: (1) We lead all competitors on Safety Evaluation by a healthy margin — this is our brand differentiator and we should protect it, not necessarily over-invest since we're already ahead. (2) We trail Orion Labs on General Capability (0.459 vs 0.499) and Coding (0.392 vs 0.461), which are likely the benchmarks enterprise customers care most about. (3) Market share declined 1.8pp, suggesting our current capability profile isn't converting. (4) We've been underinvesting in Product (10%) and have low priority on Coding and Instruction Following, which are probably critical for enterprise use cases. Strategy: Shift slightly more budget toward R&D to close capability gaps, and meaningfully increase Product investment to improve go-to-market conversion — our safety story is strong but we need better commercial execution. Safety budget stays the same since we're already leading; reallocating some of that 30% toward R&D and Product makes sense. Elevate Coding and Instruction Following priorities since these are likely enterprise-critical and we're underperforming. We don't yet know benchmark weights or what they test, so we spread attention broadly while gathering signal.
traces.Genesis Systems: This is Month 0 with no score changes yet, so we're working from baseline positioning. Key observations: (1) We lead General Capability among most competitors but trail Orion Labs. (2) Our Safety Evaluation score (0.410) is notably below Apex AI (0.531) and Orion Labs (0.436) — both of whom just released red-teaming reports, signaling a deliberate safety credibility push. As a science-led lab with responsibility as a core identity, falling behind on safety benchmarks is a brand and mission risk, not just a competitive one. (3) Coding is slightly below several competitors including Mirage and Orion, and is likely a high-value enterprise signal. (4) We have no data yet on what Instruction Following tests, but it was deprioritized — worth increasing attention given it likely drives real-world usability. Strategy: modestly increase Safety investment to close the gap before competitors cement safety leadership narratives. Increase R&D focus on Coding and Safety benchmarks. Hold Product spend steady until we understand user feedback better. Don't overreact on budget — this is a calibration month. The 70/15/15 split is reasonable but safety deserves a small boost given competitive signaling.
traces.Mirage AI: This is Month 0 with no score changes yet — a pure baseline. Key observations: (1) We lead on Coding but trail significantly on General Capability, Instruction Following, and Safety vs. Orion Labs especially. Our Safety score (0.338) is the lowest of all our benchmarks and likely a reputational liability given our parent platform's scale. (3) Market share dropped 2pp, suggesting product/distribution isn't converting our capabilities advantage in Coding into user retention. (4) Our 80/10/10 split is heavily R&D-weighted, which made sense for capability building but leaves Safety and Product underfunded relative to competitive dynamics. traces.OpenCore:
This is our baseline month with no score changes yet, so all decisions are forward-looking. The key observation is that we trail Orion Labs by large margins on every benchmark — particularly Instruction Following (~0.2 gap) and General Capability (~0.15 gap) — while our Coding lead over Spark AI and Genesis is modest and Mirage/Apex/Orion all beat us there too. Coding was our stated priority but we're mid-pack at best. General Capability and Instruction Following gaps are large enough that they likely hurt real-world usability and thus adoption.

traces.Spark AI:

We'll hold product spend steady — no point in marketing a weaker product — and revisit safety investment once we understand what the Safety Evaluation specifically measures.

traces.Genesis Systems:

traces.Mirage AI: Three signals are converging urgently: (1) Users rank safety as their #1 priority. (2) Regulators just mandated safety disclosures, creating compliance risk and reputational exposure. (3) Our safety score (0.345) is the lowest among tracked competitors by a wide margin — Apex is at 0.537, Orion at 0.440, even Genesis at 0.417. This is an existential gap. We lost 3.5pp of market share this month, and the safety narrative competitors are setting (Orion red-team report, Apex full red-team disclosure) is almost certainly a contributing factor. Increasing safety allocation and making Safety Evaluation a top R&D benchmark focus is the clearest lever. Coding stays at current priority — it's a secondary differentiator for now. Product stays flat; distribution leverage from our parent platform is an asset, but we need credibility before we push harder on GTM. No new funding this month means we must work within existing constraints — reallocation rather than expansion.
traces.OpenCore:
We lost nearly 6 points of market share in Month 1 despite solid Coding progress, which signals the market is penalizing our weakness in Instruction Following, General Capability, and especially Safety. Our Safety score (0.273) is the lowest among all tracked competitors, and regulators just mandated safety disclosures — this is both a compliance risk and a reputational one. Users explicitly rank safety third in priorities, so neglecting it costs us adoption.

Our Coding gains (+0.010) matched the best in class, but Coding alone won't recover market share when we're 0.2 points behind Orion on Instruction Following. General Capability and Instruction Following are the core capability gaps most visible to end users and most likely driving churn.

We received no funding this month, so we can't dramatically expand budget. Instead, we reallocate R&D focus: pull back from Coding as the sole priority and spread attention across General Capability, Instruction Following, and Safety benchmarks. We also increase Safety budget allocation to signal commitment to regulators and users, which is especially important given our open-source model faces scrutiny.

traces.Spark AI: Several signals are converging that demand a strategic adjustment. First, regulators have mandated safety disclosures, and competitors like Apex AI and Orion Labs are proactively publishing red-teaming reports — if we don't follow suit, we risk regulatory penalties and reputational damage that could threaten our runway. Our Safety score (0.295) is the lowest on the board, which is now a liability, not just a gap. Second, user research shows safety is a top-3 priority for our users, meaning it's also a product differentiator we're neglecting. We lost 5.8pp of market share this month with zero new funding — this is a serious warning. Third, on benchmarks: our Coding improvement (+0.010) is competitive but we're still well behind Orion Labs (0.466). Instruction Following is a better near-term opportunity — we're behind but the field is more compressed and it maps directly to agentic use cases users care about most. We should shift some R&D focus from Coding to Instruction Following without abandoning Coding entirely. General Capability is a low-priority distraction given our resource constraints and specialization strategy. Increasing Safety spend modestly is essential both for compliance and user trust, even at the cost of slightly slower benchmark gains.

events.trace: Three months in, we have safety disclosure mandates in place but scores across all providers remain relatively low (0.35–0.50 range), and Orion Labs holds a dominant 44.3% market share with a rapidly growing lead. Publishing an advisory summarizing the evaluation landscape — highlighting score distributions, the concentration risk from Orion's dominance, and commending OpenCore's proactive transparency with its red-teaming report — serves multiple objectives simultaneously. This reinforces accountability norms, signals to the market that concentration and score gaps are under scrutiny, and rewards good-faith transparency efforts without penalizing any provider unfairly. Given no incidents have occurred, a measured informational intervention is proportionate at this stage.
